accepted.question_text: Let pi: X -> C^n be a ramified Riemann domain, where X is a possibly singular reduced complex space and pi is a holomorphic map whose fibers pi^{-1}({z}) are discrete for every z in C^n. Assume that for every point a in C^n there exists a neighborhood U of a such that pi^{-1}(U) is Stein, so X is locally Stein over C^n. Under these assumptions, what sufficient conditions or what necessary conditions guarantee that X itself is Stein? The paper states that this problem remains open even when X is non-singular.
accepted.context_brief: Levi problem for locally Stein ramified Riemann domains over C^n

evidence.quote: Problem. Let pi : X -> Cn be a ramified Riemann domain (cf. the beginning of §1). Assume that for every point a in Cn there is a neighborhood U of a in Cn such that pi^{-1}U is Stein (locally Stein). Find sufficient or necessary conditions for X to be Stein.
The problem above is open even for non-singular X (cf. [23] for some affirmative result).

We will employ commonly used notion and terminologies in analytic function theory of several variables without definitions ... except for a Riemann domain X over Cn ... which in the present note is a possibly singular reduced complex space X together with a holomorphic map pi : X -> Cn ... such that the fibers pi^{-1}{z} are discrete for all z in Cn.
